objective: Prove that after the doubling law at every lag for k lags and a stop, every reading of an original ring from then on (the lags at which a contact needs it, with or without freezes) is the fixed (3 * 2^k)-torus's from an open first row, so the cut length, the time length and the plain first need between original rings are that torus's, the original rings 2^k ring steps apart per original step; check it at the cell level for k = 1, 2 at g = 2 and 3; and compute what slower schedules (doubling every 2 to 4 lags, k doublings) read after a stop against the same torus.
status: Proved 2026-11-10 (by hand, from the transfer lemma; checked at the cell level; slower schedules computed): after the doubling law at every lag for k lags and a stop, every need of every ring, with or without freezes from the stop on, is the fixed (n 2^k x m 2^k)-torus's, so the stopped plane reads that torus's cut length, time length and plain first need, its original rings 2^k ring steps apart per original step. Schedules whose rings heard each other before the stop do not read the fixed torus (computed).
title: A grown plane that stops reads the fixed torus's distances, scaled by the growth
